---
title: "Setup guide"
---

This sets up everything you need for the semester: Git, Positron (the editor),
uv (which builds the course's Python environment), and your private course repo
on GitHub. Do it before the second class session. If you get stuck, see the
[Setup FAQ](setup-faq.qmd).

**Before you start:** about 5 GB of free disk space, an internet connection, and
your WSU login. On a Chromebook or iPad, skip to [No-install path](#no-install).

## Steps

1. **GitHub**: the website that stores your course work online. Each student gets a private repository ("repo") there, a folder only you and the instructor can see. New problem sets arrive in it. To hand in work, you use Git to save it to your repo, then submit the link to it in Canvas.
   - Sign up at [github.com](https://github.com) with any username (it doesn't need to be your real name), and add your WSU email to the account.
   - Apply for GitHub Education student benefits at [education.github.com](https://education.github.com). Approval can take a few days; it gives you free GitHub Copilot and free Codespaces hours.
   - Enter your GitHub username in the Canvas "GitHub username" survey, so your course repo can be created.

2. **Git**: version-control software. It saves snapshots ("commits") of your work and syncs them with your private course repo on GitHub. You'll use it to get each new problem set (pull) and to hand in your work (commit and push), mostly through buttons in Positron. You'll type Git commands in Positron's terminal only during setup and for the occasional fix.
   - *Windows:* install "Git for Windows" from [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com) and accept every default. It includes the sign-in helper Git needs for GitHub.
   - *Mac:* open Terminal, type `git --version`, and accept the prompt to install the Command Line Tools. Then install the GitHub CLI from
     [cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com) and run `gh auth login` (choose the web-browser login) and `gh auth setup-git`, so Git can sign in to GitHub.

3. **Positron** (free, from Posit): the program where you'll do all your coding. It opens your course repo, runs Python notebooks and scripts, shows your data and plots, and has Git built in. Download and install it from [positron.posit.co](https://positron.posit.co).
   - When you first open your course folder, Positron asks whether you trust the authors of the files. Click **Yes, I trust the authors**; it's your own repo.
   - If Positron offers to create a Python environment, decline. Step 8 builds the course environment instead.
   - If Positron asks "Would you like Positron to periodically run git fetch?", click **Yes**. It checks GitHub for new problem sets without changing your files; a small down-arrow count in the status bar means something new is ready to pull.
   - The first time you commit, Positron may ask whether to stage all your changes and commit them directly. Click **Yes** (or **Always**).
   - The first time you click **Sync Changes**, Positron asks you to confirm pulling and pushing. Click **OK** (or **OK, Don't Ask Again**).
   - If Positron asks you to sign in to GitHub, your browser will show "Authorize Visual-Studio-Code". That's expected: Positron is built on VS Code. If Positron then says sign-in failed, see the [Setup FAQ](setup-faq.qmd).
   - If Positron offers to turn on an AI assistant or code completions, skip it for now. AI autocomplete stays off through Week 5 (see [Policies](policies.qmd)).

4. **uv**: a free tool that installs Python and the course packages, so everyone's setup is identical. To install it, open a terminal: in Positron, choose **Terminal > New Terminal** (on Windows this opens PowerShell; on a Mac, a regular terminal). Then paste the command for your system and press Enter:
   - *Windows:*

     ```powershell
     powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
     ```

   - *Mac:*

     ```bash
     curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
     ```
   - Not using Positron's terminal? On Windows, click Start, type **PowerShell**, and open **Windows PowerShell**. On a Mac, press **Cmd+Space**, type **Terminal**, and press Return.
   - When it finishes, quit and reopen Positron (or close and reopen the terminal) so it can find uv. Check with `uv --version`, which should print a version number.

5. **Tell Git who you are.** In a terminal, paste each command, replace the text in quotes with your own name and the email on your GitHub account, then press Enter:

   ```bash
   git config --global user.name "First Last"
   ```

   ```bash
   git config --global user.email "your-github-email@example.com"
   ```
   
6. **Accept your repo invitation** from the email GitHub sends you, or at
   `https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>/invitations`.

7. **Clone your repo.** Make a folder such as `EconS431` directly in your home
   folder (`C:\Users\<you>\EconS431` or `/Users/<you>/EconS431`). **Not in
   OneDrive, Dropbox, or iCloud, and not on your Desktop or in Documents**, which
   many laptops sync automatically. Then, in a Positron terminal:

   ```
   cd ~/EconS431
   git clone https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>.git
   ```

   The first clone opens a GitHub sign-in window; choose the browser option.
   Then open the new folder: **File > Open Folder** > `EconS431/ps-<your-username>`.
8. **Build the environment.** In a Positron terminal inside your repo, run
   `uv sync`. Then click the interpreter name at the top right and choose the
   Python from `.venv` (labeled **econs431**). If Positron offers to create an
   environment, decline: `uv sync` builds the course one.
9. **Check it.** Run `uv run python check_setup.py`. Every line should start with
   `[OK]`. Then open `ps01/ps01.ipynb`, choose the same **econs431** kernel at the
   top right of the notebook, complete it, commit, push, and submit the commit
   link in Canvas.

## No-install path {#no-install}

For a Chromebook, an iPad, or a laptop that won't cooperate: do steps 1 and 6.
Then, on your repo's GitHub page, click **Code > Codespaces > Create codespace**.
Wait for setup to finish (a few minutes the first time) and start at step 9.

## Every problem set

1. **Pull** in Positron (Source Control > **...** > Pull). The new `psNN/` folder appears.
2. **Work** in `psNN/psNN.ipynb`, and commit whenever something works.
3. **Restart & Run All.** If it doesn't run from top to bottom, it isn't finished.
4. **Fill in the AI usage note** at the bottom.
5. **Push, copy the commit URL** from GitHub, and **paste it into Canvas** before
   the deadline.

## Rules of the road

- Your repo is private. Never make it public or share it, even after the course,
  unless an assignment says it may be shared.
- Use relative paths (`data/prices.csv`), never `C:\Users\...`. Your code must
  run on the instructor's machine.
- Don't commit `.venv/` or big data files. GitHub rejects files over 100 MB, and
  your repo's `.gitignore` handles the common cases.
- Don't change `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`. If you think you need another
  package, ask on Discussions.
- **Asking for help:** see [Getting help](setup-faq.qmd#getting-help).
